L0101.text: Once, a machine learned to see.
L0101.spoken: Once, a machine learned to see.

L0102.text: Its eye: four hundred light cells, twenty by twenty.
L0102.spoken: Its eye: four hundred light cells, twenty by twenty.

L0103.text: Behind it, wires, and racks of dials that motors turned.
L0103.spoken: Behind it, wires, and racks of dials that motors turned.

L0104.text: It was the Mark I Perceptron, the project of psychologist Frank Rosenblatt.
L0104.spoken: It was the Mark One Perceptron, the project of psychologist Frank Rosenblatt.

L0105.text: Nobody gave it the rule. Show it a shape; it guesses.
L0105.spoken: Nobody gave it the rule. Show it a shape; it guesses.

L0105b.text: Each lit cell tugs the needle through the dials it feeds; the total decides.
L0105b.spoken: Each lit cell tugs the needle through the dials it feeds; the total decides.

L0106.text: When it guesses wrong, motors nudge the dials that had a say, a little, toward the right answer.
L0106.spoken: When it guesses wrong, motors nudge the dials that had a say, a little, toward the right answer.

L0107.text: Wrong, and wrong again, and then, quite suddenly... right.
L0107.spoken: Wrong, and wrong again, and then, quite suddenly... right.

L0108.text: It could learn only simple patterns. In 1969, Minsky and Papert showed just how simple; for years, interest faded. Its descendants, today's neural networks, still learn from mistakes.
L0108.spoken: It could learn only simple patterns. In nineteen sixty-nine, Minsky and Pappert showed just how simple; for years, interest faded. Its descendants, today's neural networks, still learn from mistakes.
